content: 1. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. 2. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of transdermal buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 3. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the cabazitaxel dose by 25%. 4. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is required, reduce the cabozantinib dose by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx). Resume the previous dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 5. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 7. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining these drugs for 2 weeks before and during ketoconazole use if possible. Monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly. 8. Ketoconazole increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the ceritinib dose by approximately 33%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor. 9. Chlorpromazine and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Consider reducing the cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily. 11. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Clarithromycin and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Ketoconazole also increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Clomipramine and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 15. Ketoconazole decreases the effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Clopidogrel efficacy may be reduced by drugs that inhibit CYP2C19, as its antiplatelet activity depends on an active metabolite formed via CYP2C19. 16. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of clozapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with drugs that are both P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If coadministration is necessary, reduce the colchicine dose or frequency as recommended in prescribing information. Use of colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 20. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens (vaginal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 22. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of cortisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Ketoconazole increases the levels of crizotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Refer to prescribing information for precise dosage modifications. 24. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. For atrial fibrillation, reduce the dabigatran dose if CrCl is 30–50 mL/min. Avoid coadministration if CrCl <30 mL/min. For DVT/PE treatment, avoid coadministration if CrCl <50 mL/min. 25. Ketoconazole increases the levels of dabrafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 26. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of daridorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of darifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Ketoconazole and darunavir mutually increase each other's effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Specific dosage recommendations for ketoconazole are not available when coadministered with darunavir. 29. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 30. Desipramine and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 32. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Dofetilide and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Doxepin and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Droperidol and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 37. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. 38. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of elacestrant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of elbasvir/grazoprevir with certain strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 40. Ketoconazole increases the levels of eletriptan by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Separate administration by 72 hours. 41. Ketoconazole increases the levels of eluxadoline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the eluxadoline dose to 75 mg PO BID if coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors. 42. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to 150 mg/day if the current dose is 450 mg/day, or to 75 mg/day if the current dose is 150–300 mg/day. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. 43. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of entrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib, a CYP3A4 substrate. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. 44. Enzalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of ketoconazole with strong CYP3A4 inducers from 2 weeks before and during treatment with ketoconazole tablets. If use is unavoidable, monitor antifungal activity and increase ketoconazole dosage if necessary. 45. Epinephrine and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Racemic epinephrine and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 47. Ketoconazole increases the levels of eplerenone by decreasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by altering its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4/CYP2C9 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider decreasing the dose accordingly. If the strong inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the erdafitinib dose in the absence of drug-related toxicities. 49. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If use is unavoidable, monitor for erlotinib toxicities. 50. Ketoconazole increases the levels of erlotinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 51. Erythromycin base and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 52. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 53. Erythromycin lactobionate and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 54. Erythromycin stearate and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 55. Esomeprazole decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of etrasimod by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Increased exposure to etrasimod is observed when coadministered with a moderate-to-strong inhibitor of both CYP2C9 and CYP3A4. 57. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of everolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. 58. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 59. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fedratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day. 60. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of felodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 61. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fesoterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 62. Ketoconazole decreases the levels or effects of fexinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor fexinidazole for decreased efficacy due to reduced plasma concentrations of active M1 and M2 metabolites. 63. Fluconazole and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 64. Fluphenazine and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 65. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of intranasal fluticasone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic corticosteroid adverse effects; monitor for signs/symptoms of high corticosteroid concentrations, including Cushing-type signs/symptoms. 66. Formoterol and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 67. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Dose reduction of ketoconazole may be needed for patients receiving >400 mg ketoconazole daily. When coadministered with fosamprenavir with ritonavir, ketoconazole doses >200 mg/day are not recommended. 68. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of fosaprepitant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 69. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of futibatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of futibatinib with drugs that are dual P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the incidence/severity of futibatinib toxicities. 70. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of gilteritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Consider alternatives to any strong CYP3A4 inhibitor when coadministered with gilteritinib. If such a combination cannot be avoided, closely monitor for gilteritinib-related adverse effects. Interrupt and reduce gilteritinib dosage in patients with serious or life-threatening toxicity. 71. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of glasdegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative therapies that are not strong CYP3A inhibitors or monitor for increased risk of adverse effects, including QTc interval prolongation. 72. Haloperidol and ketoconazole both increase the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 73. Ketoconazole increases the levels of ibrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
